I build AI workflows and the guardrails that keep them honest, and I want to do that at CivicPlus. Your AI Enablement Engineer role sits where product operations meet practical AI implementation. That is where I have spent the last few years, building internal tools that work inside real constraints, including regulated data and cross-functional teams.

At Redwood, I built FlareGuard, an AI content validation suite that cut escalations by 70-80% by catching bad output before it reached customers. I redesigned a 200-article help portal with role-aware navigation and automated the documentation pipeline with Playwright screenshot capture. At Bird, I migrated 500+ Zendesk articles to conditional content and built the release notes pipeline. That work is prompt design, evaluation, and system integration, and I have the Python, API, and LLM experience to extend it beyond documentation.

CivicPlus serves local government, so the margin for error is thin. I am comfortable with that. I know how to build AI-enabled workflows, document them clearly, and measure whether they actually work. I would welcome the conversation.
